name: detect-entities
summary: Extract named entities (person, organization, location, misc) from free text using a real DistilBERT-NER model forward pass.
description: Runs a real DistilBERT (dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0) token-classification forward pass -- WordPiece tokenize (case-preserving; capitalization is real signal for this model), 6 transformer layers, per-token BIO-tag classification, then merge adjacent B-/I- tags of the same type into entity spans with byte offsets into the input text. Returns an array of {text, label, start, end} (label one of PER, ORG, LOC, MISC; start/end are UTF-8 byte offsets). A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or a 'leading capitalized word' heuristic. Known limitation, faithfully reproduced rather than hidden: this compact model sometimes tags interior WordPieces of a multi-piece entity with a fresh B- tag instead of a continuing I- tag, which this capability's BIO merge (correctly) reports as separate adjacent entities rather than guessing they should be one -- e.g. 'Acme Corp' can come back as three short spans. Does not resolve entities against a knowledge base, deduplicate mentions, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want person, organization, and location entities extracted from a sentence, so that a caller can build a structured summary without a keyword list.

input_example.text: Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want a well-known person, organization, and location correctly grouped into single clean spans when the model tags them consistently, so that common cases read naturally.

input_example.text: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want text with no named entities to return an empty array rather than a forced guess, so that ordinary sentences aren't mislabeled.

input_example.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want empty input to return an empty array rather than an error, so that an empty upstream field never breaks the pipeline.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: Each entity's start/end are UTF-8 byte offsets into the exact input text string, and entities[i].text equals input.text[start..end].
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces an entity array in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#465, follow-up to #455/#460 (third spec 001 FR-017 agent). Motivated by a traverse-framework/reference-apps survey finding the same task -- classify/extract entities from free text -- implemented independently, rule-based, in doc-approval.analyze's docType, traverse-starter.process's noteType, and meeting-notes.process's owner extraction (self-disclosed as 'not production-grade named-entity recognition'). meeting-notes.process is additionally the one capability with governed two-app reuse in that repo (docs/two-app-reuse-contract.md). Reuses the #![no_std] BERT-encoder engine proven in report.translate-fr-semantic.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/text-detect-entities: 19 #[test] cases (NER1 header parse, multi-byte char/byte offset tracking, case-preserving WordPiece split/OOV/sequence-cap, forward-pass finiteness/determinism, label/entity-type mapping, BIO merge incl. dangling-I-without-B and mismatched-type cases, empty/missing-text defaults) against a synthetic fixture; cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=97.13%, regions=96.35%. Separately verified end to end against the real published ONNX graph (dslim/distilbert-NER onnx/model.onnx) via onnxruntime: DistilBERT's per-layer weight *matrices* are exported as anonymous onnx::MatMul_<n> tensors (only biases are named), resolved by tracing each layer's named .bias through its consuming Add node to the feeding MatMul rather than trusting initializer list order; numpy reference matched real-model logits to 6 decimal places on an arbitrary token sequence, and produced semantically correct PER/ORG/LOC tags on real sentences (e.g. 'Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.'). Quantization tested: 0/65 label (argmax) mismatches across 5 varied sentences before/after int8 -- unlike the recurrent Silero VAD (registry#460) this is a stateless feedforward call, so quantization noise doesn't compound. Ran the built --features full-model artifact under wasmtime: entity spans matched the quantized Python reference exactly, byte offset for byte offset, on multiple test sentences. Cross-arch (x86_64 vs aarch64) byte-identity was NOT verified -- no x86_64 host or emulator was available in the authoring environment -- hence risk.determinism_class: model_derived rather than deterministic (spec 024). License: dslim/distilbert-NER is Apache-2.0, verified directly against the model's Hugging Face API metadata (cardData.license, license:apache-2.0 tag).
